title: Don't Get Spooked: Stocks Could Still Soar in Q4
author: Not Specified
description: October's market volatility has been driven by inflation concerns and AI financing debates, particularly CoreWeave's financial struggles. However, the market correction appears contained to tech themes rather than broad-based panic. Entering the historically strongest nine-month stretch of the presidential cycle (Q4 midterm through Q2 pre-election year), markets face headwinds from elevated valuations and high interest rates, though strong earnings growth and AI's transformative potential could support gains.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Nvidia holds ~10% stake in CoreWeave and CEO publicly defended CoreWeave's financial strength, suggesting confidence. However, semiconductor index extended losing streak to eight consecutive sessions, indicating sector weakness despite management reassurance.
Carrying roughly $50 billion in debt, CoreWeave fell painfully last week and has become the market's proxy for AI financing concerns. CEO Huang's public defense suggests financial stress.
Meta reports earnings this week. While S&P 500 tracking strong 24.6% earnings growth, the article provides no specific guidance on Meta's performance.

title: Breakfast News: A $5.7 Billion Flex or Genius?
author: Tmf Breakfast News
description: Salesforce acquires Braze for $5.7 billion to strengthen its marketing capabilities, with Braze stock jumping 50%. Netflix faces growth challenges with slowing revenue and weak ad performance. SpaceX beats expectations with 161% revenue growth, while Intuitive Surgical falls despite beating estimates due to cooling U.S. procedure growth. Tesla, Meta, and IBM report earnings with major capital spending decisions in focus. EQT continues steady cash flow growth as a natural gas producer.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Acquisition of Braze is strategically sound and relatively inexpensive, but long-term growth prospects are limited to 7-10% annually rather than historical 20%, suggesting modest upside potential.
Stock surged 51% on acquisition announcement; company has strong financials with $300M+ net cash, improving margins, and 25%+ annual topline growth at reasonable valuation.
Stock fell 6% after hours due to slowing revenue growth (12%, slowest in 3 years), weak ad revenue below targets, and minimal viewing hour growth (2%), indicating fundamental growth challenges.
Stock fell 7% despite beating earnings estimates because U.S. da Vinci procedure growth slowed to 10%, lagging overseas growth and signaling weakening domestic demand momentum.

title: Bloom Energy vs. Vistra: Which Energy Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
author: Sara Appino
description: The article compares Bloom Energy, a fast-growing clean-energy company specializing in fuel cell systems for AI data centers, against Vistra, a diversified utility giant with 44,000 megawatts of generation capacity. Bloom Energy is recommended as the better buy for 2026 due to its explosive Q2 growth (166% revenue increase, $1B quarterly revenue milestone) and strong momentum in the AI infrastructure market, despite higher valuation multiples and execution risks. Vistra is acknowledged as a solid, well-executing company with steady performance and diversified assets, but lacks the dynamic growth trajectory of Bloom.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong Q2 2026 results with 166% YoY revenue growth, first $1B quarterly revenue milestone, EPS doubling analyst estimates, and management guidance raise. Explosive demand from AI data centers and expanding backlog demonstrate significant growth momentum, though offset by high valuation multiples (P/E 303.38) and execution risks.

Solid operational execution with 30%+ YoY adjusted EBITDA growth and strategic partnerships (KKR, Nvidia). Diversified generation portfolio and stable utility business provide steady performance, but modest revenue growth (3% YoY) and lower valuation (P/E 25.37) reflect mature, slower-growth profile compared to Bloom.

title: Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) Stock Plummeted 13% Last Week. Should You Buy the Dip Before Nov. 3?
author: Anthony Di Pizio
description: AMD stock fell 13% last week amid concerns about AI funding challenges and potential slowdown in data center chip demand. While AMD has closed the performance gap with Nvidia through its MI450 GPUs, the company's stock is priced for perfection at a P/E ratio of 91.8—over three times higher than Nvidia's 27.1. Ahead of AMD's Nov. 3 earnings report, the analyst remains cautious due to elevated valuation and uncertainty in the AI industry, despite AMD's strong growth prospects.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Stock plummeted 13% due to AI funding concerns and potential demand slowdown. Despite strong MI450 GPU performance and growth prospects, the company is priced for perfection at a P/E of 91.8, making it overvalued relative to Nvidia and vulnerable to disappointment.
